pr_body:
This changes ILLink's `MethodProxy`, `MethodReturnValue`, `ParameterProxy` (which provides the static type of `MethodParameterValue`), and `FieldValue` to track generic instantiations, whenever they refer to instantiated generic methods, or methods/fields on instantiated generic types.

To support this, the proxy types now store `MethodReference`/`FieldReference` instead of `MethodDefinition`/`FieldDefinition`. The cecil object model doesn't automatically "inflate" parameter/return-value/field types, so this includes logic to do the generic substitution in our proxy types.

`MethodProxy` provides information that's only available on cecil's `MethodDefinition`, so it has been changed to store both a `MethodReference` and the resolved `MethodDefinition`.

The logic to inflate generic types is extended to include support for types that use method generic parameters.

It may be helpful to review commit-by-commit.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/105345
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/93719

issue_context.title: Method body scanner cannot determine static type of return value from IEnumerator<T>.get_Current
comments: https://github.com/mono/linker/pull/2028 adds a test for this case

Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-reflection See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Repro: ```C# [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(PublicMethods)] class AnnotatedBase { } void Test(IEnumerable instances) { foreach (AnnotatedBase instance in instances) { instance.GetType().GetMethod("Test"); // Warns: IL2075 } } ``` The problem is that the `instance` value is evaluated as a return value from `IEnumerator.get_Current()`. Linker will not correctly resolve that type (which is declared as a generic parameter) and will end up analyzing `instance` as not having a known static type. This is a general problem with ability to resolve type of a generic parameter given a proper instantiation.

review_comments: Should we do an 'as' cast or type check rather than a cast here? Or do we know for sure that the `genericInstanceProvider` will be either a `GenericInstanceType` or `GenericInstanceMethod`?
The only cecil types that implement IGenericInstance are GenericInstanceType and GenericInstanceMethod - I added an assert to make it more clear that we're relying on this.
